pr_title: [WIP] Allow rake tasks to be loaded without rails
pr_body:
### Summary

Allow Active Record's rake tasks to be loaded without Rails. There are other references to Rails in database tasks, but these are the only one blocking setting up databases on https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/35902.

I think migrations and rollbacks should also work, so I'll try to fix those too:

### TODO:

- [ ] Fix `rake db:migrate`
- [ ] Fix `rake db:rollback`


Closes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/35902.
pr_comments: Closing this since I merged https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/36023

issue_context.title: ActiveRecord::Tasks::DatabaseTasks no longer works outside of Rails
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
Clone example project from https://github.com/jhollinger/rake-record and use the **activerecord-6** branch.

    bundle install
    bundle exec rake db:setup
    NameError: uninitialized constant ActiveRecord::Tasks::DatabaseTasks::Rails 
    ...

### Expected behavior
With proper configuration (i.e. manually setting `db_dir`, `root`, `migrations_paths`, `database_configuration`, etc) `ActiveRecord::Tasks::DatabaseTasks` should be usable when `Rails` is not defined. This works as expected in the master branch of the above project (on Rails 5.X).

    bundle install
    bundle exec rake db:setup
    Created database 'data/development.sqlite3'
    -- create_table("widgets", {:force=>:cascade})
       -> 0.0122s


### Actual behavior
Calls to `DatabaseTasks.for_each` (such as those made in `lib/active_record/railties/databases.rake`) raise:

    NameError: uninitialized constant ActiveRecord::Tasks::DatabaseTasks::Rails

In recent Rails 4- 5 this file has always wrapped things in `if defined? Rails`, but there are now a few `Rails` references outside of those checks.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.0.beta3

**Ruby version**: 2.5.1p57
comments: @douglasrosa0110 I'm not sure I understand. The `rails` command certainly wouldn't work w/o the rails gem.
hmmm, that is true since the multi-database support in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/32274. @eileencodes do you think we can decouple those tasks from the `railtie` framework?

I believe `Rails.env` can be subbed out for `ActiveRecord::ConnectionHandling::DEFAULT_ENV.call` but I'm not sure about `Rails.application.config.database_configuration`, we might have to conditionally call that if Rails is defined and use something else otherwise.
I've been out this week but can look at this early next week.

review_comments:
I can see why you're passing the empty array here since `build_configs_will` just return the empty array.  But given that it will return just an empty array we know that the rest of this function will just no-op, perhaps it's better to just have a guard clause here: `return unless defined?(Rails)`. 

I think a better approach might be even to have something like: 

``` ruby
databases = if defined?(Rails) ? Rails.application.config.load_database_yaml  : database_configuration

return unless databases
```

That way if someone has set the `database_configuration` accessor we use it, instead of having a empty array, and we also return early if no configuration is set.

I wanted to followup here - when loading these tasks `database_configuration` will always be `nil` because they are loaded before the application is booted and therefore before Railties loads `database_configuration` into Active Record. In my PR I chose to just ignore the multi-db tasks altogether unless Rails is defined.
